title: Coily hair, wash day and a clean, safe workstation

say: Coily hair, wash day, and a clean, safe workstation.
This is the video for module one of Hair Care and Simple Styling.
Afro-textured hair is not hard or bad hair. The part you see is dead protein called keratin, so once it is damaged, it cannot heal. Prevention is everything.

panel.heading: Beautiful hair, fragile at every bend
items: Hair is dead keratin: damage cannot heal
Sebum struggles past the bends, so ends stay dry
Every bend is a weak point where hair snaps
Three rules: moisture, gentle detangling, low tension

say: On tightly coiled hair, the scalp's natural oil, sebum, struggles to travel past each bend, so the ends stay dry.

say: For example, Amaka in Onitsha takes down Blessing's braids after seven weeks, and Blessing is worried by the hair in the comb.
Shed hairs have a tiny white bulb at the root end. Some shedding every day is normal, and braids trap it.

panel.heading: Shedding or breakage?
left: Tiny white bulb at the root end
Normal part of the growth cycle
Trapped in braids, so it looks a lot

say: Short pieces with no bulb are broken. Most came from the nape, where the braids were smallest and driest. So next time, Amaka makes the nape braids looser and slightly bigger.

say: Wash about once every one to two weeks. Step one. Divide the hair into four to six sections, to prevent matting.

panel.heading: The wash-day order
items: Section the hair into four to six parts
Shampoo the scalp with finger pads, not nails
Condition the length and ends
Detangle: fingers, then a wide-tooth comb
Rinse cool or lukewarm, blot with a T-shirt
Moisturise and seal with LOC or LCO

say: Step two. Shampoo the scalp with the pads of your fingers, not your nails, and let the lather run down the length.

say: Step three. Put conditioner on the length and ends, and leave it for the time on the label.

say: This is the rule. Start at the ends and work up to the roots. Never comb coily hair dry.

say: Step five. Rinse with cool or lukewarm water, then blot with a cotton T-shirt instead of rubbing.

say: Step six. Moisturise and seal. Water is the true moisturiser; oils and butters slow water loss.
LOC means liquid, then oil, then cream. Low porosity hair often prefers LCO, with oil last.

say: Combs, clips and towels can carry lice, ringworm and bacteria from head to head. After every client, remove all hair from your tools.

panel.heading: Clean first, then disinfect
items: Remove all hair from combs and brushes
Wash with soap, scrub between the teeth
Soak in disinfectant for the label time
Remove with gloves, air dry on a clean towel
Store covered, never with used tools

say: Wash them in warm water with liquid soap, scrubbing between the teeth with an old toothbrush.

say: Cleaning comes first, because disinfectant cannot work through grease and hair.

say: Then fully soak the tools in a salon disinfectant mixed exactly as the label says. Barbicide's label contact time is 10 minutes. For other products, follow their label.

say: With household bleach, dilute exactly as the bottle says, mix fresh each day, wear gloves and open a window. Never mix it with ammonia, vinegar or other cleaners.

Hot water in a stable bowl, never the kettle over her. Towel on her shoulders, children away.
Lice, scaly patches, sores or pus: stop kindly, suggest a clinic, disinfect every tool.

say: To seal braid ends, pour hot water into a stable bowl. Never hold the kettle over the client, and keep children away.

say: Here is a worked example. Ngozi in Enugu wants to braid on Saturdays in her parlour, with about 30,000 naira to spend.
Combs and clips cost about 6,000 naira. Three capes and six towels, so she can rotate them, cost about 12,000.

say: A lidded container and disinfectant cost about 9,000, and she keeps 3,000 for soap, gloves and a lidded bin. Prices are approximate.

say: To remember. Prevention is everything. Keep to moisture, gentle detangling and low tension. Water hydrates, oils seal. Clean before you disinfect. And never style over signs of infection.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Damage cannot heal, so prevention is everything
Moisture, gentle detangling and low tension
Water hydrates; oils and butters seal
Always clean before you disinfect
Stop the service if you see signs of infection
